gen-dafont-bloody-gf-noto-sans-mro: Commanding up top, with Bloody's big round bowls doing the shouting. Noto Sans Mro goes dense and tall through the middle of each word, with generous entrances into every letter.
gen-dafont-bloody-gf-noto-sans-multani: Bloody's big round lowercase bowls are the first thing you notice, heavy and loud. Noto Sans Multani counters with a lofty x-height and an e whose terminal gapes wide, which gives the pairing its strongest hook.
gen-dafont-bloody-gf-noto-sans-myanmar: Loud, round and a bit menacing, Bloody sets the mood with its big bowls. Noto Sans Myanmar follows with a heavy-looking strip of text and a broad c, so give it the larger size.
gen-dafont-bloody-gf-noto-sans-nabataean: Commanding, Bloody swells with big round bowls. Noto Sans Nabataean stands its lowercase almost cap-tall and curves its s wide open, so a long stretch of text moves briskly and stays easy on the eye.
gen-dafont-bloody-gf-noto-sans-nag-munda: Big round bowls, loud and gory: that is Bloody. And Noto Sans Nag Mundari sits beside it with half-unwrapped c and s shapes and lowercase that nearly rivals its capitals, a quieter sort of sans-serif confidence.
gen-dafont-bloody-gf-noto-sans-nandinaga: Approachable is the surprise here, since Noto Sans Nandinagari keeps its openings generous at every weight under Bloody's big round bowls. Their strongest quality is the shout and the welcome.
gen-dafont-bloody-gf-noto-sans-newa: Noto Sans Newa reads open and tall, its lowercase e plainly gaping. Bloody's big round bowls hit hard above it, and the sans below keeps the tall counters doing the quiet work of carrying the text.
gen-dafont-bloody-gf-noto-sans-nushu: Bloody's big round lowercase bowls are what you see first, and they look commanding. Noto Sans Nushu has a towering x-height and terminals held far from the stroke, which is where the body font does its best work.
gen-dafont-bloody-gf-noto-sans-ogham: Noto Sans Ogham has wide gaps in its e and lowercase bodies so tall they look bold. Bloody roars above it in big round bowls.
gen-dafont-bloody-gf-noto-sans-ol-chiki: Clean and contemporary below, with curve tails held well back from the body, Noto Sans Ol Chiki makes words read as solid blocks. But Bloody above it is all big round bowls and commanding swagger, a plain sans against a loud display.
